This is the planned structure of the chapter, published so the curriculum can be reviewed before the prose is written. Each heading below becomes a section; the last section is what you will build and test. About 55 minutes when written.

1.1 · From a product goal to a measurable property

the user, the task, and what a failure costs.

1.2 · Metric trees

one north-star outcome, the drivers under it, and the guardrails beside it.

1.3 · Error analysis first

read 100 outputs, cluster the failures, then decide what to measure.

1.4 · The eval-driven development loop

hypothesis, change, measure, keep or revert.

1.5 · Worked example

defining "good" for a support assistant, in four failure modes.

What you build

An error-analysis notebook that turns 100 raw outputs into a failure taxonomy with counts. Every number it produces is asserted by a test, and the chapter's companion notebook recomputes it.
